title: Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India

content.caseIdentity: Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India, (1999) 2 SCC 228
content.facts: The Supreme Court considered a dispute requiring interpretation of the governing family-law provision or closely connected statutory rule.
questionsBeforeCourt: What is the correct legal interpretation and application of the governing statutory rule?
content.ratioDecidendi: 'After him' in s. 6(a) does not make the mother legally incapable of being a natural guardian during the father's lifetime; the provision must be read consistently with equality and the child's welfare.
content.holding: 'After him' in s. 6(a) does not make the mother legally incapable of being a natural guardian during the father's lifetime; the provision must be read consistently with equality and the child's welfare.
